title: Naval on Tim Ferriss: guard your time, build habits, and play the long game in startups
summary: Naval answers Reddit questions on AI, the gig economy, happiness, habits and early-career startup advice. The business-relevant parts: build an independent brand, go to the startup hub, expect individual ventures to fail but keep taking shots, distrust investor advice because incentives rule, and guard your time fiercely.

principles.text: Prepare for the future of work by building an independent brand under your own name around something you love and can be best at.
principles.quote: Build an independent brand around it, with your name, not a company’s name or other people’s names around it.

principles.text: Keep doing new, creative work; anything non-creative gets replicated by society and you stop being paid full value.
principles.quote: Anything that’s not a creative, society can replicate and then not pay you full value over time, so it’s always better to solve new problems and do new things

principles.text: To break into startups, move to the hub where everyone is and be willing to do any work; you'll find your way within a couple of years.
principles.quote: Startups are a moved forward by people who are just willing to do the work.

principles.text: Individual ventures often fail but entrepreneurs rarely do if they keep taking shots; early wins teach the wrong lessons.
principles.quote: individual entrepreneurial efforts often fail, but individual entrepreneurs over their careers rarely fail. As long as you can keep taking shots on goal, and you keep getting back up, eventually you’ll get through.

principles.text: Be skeptical of investors' advice to founders because it is self-serving; incentives drive everything.
principles.quote: investors giving advice is always self-serving advice. Don’t take your advice from investors if you can help it, because they have their particular view of the world

principles.text: Guard your time ruthlessly: leave empty space for thinking and serendipity, and say no unless it is a hell yes.
principles.quote: I think you have to be pretty ruthless about saying no to things, about turning people down, and about leaving room in your life for serendipity.
